Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate Ministry of Public Security Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Criminal Cases of "Debt-Trap Loans"

Fa Fa [2019] No. 11

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate, Public Security Bureau, and Justice Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In order to continue to deepen the special campaign to combat organized crime and root out local mafia, and to accurately identify and severely punish in accordance with the law criminals involved in "debt-trap loans", the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice have jointly issued the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Criminal Cases of 'Debt-Trap Loans'". Please conscientiously implement these opinions.

February 28, 2019

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Criminal Cases of "Debt-Trap Loans"

In order to continue to deepen the special campaign to combat organized crime and root out local mafia, and to accurately identify and severely punish in accordance with the law criminals involved in "debt-trap loans", the following opinions are hereby put forward on several issues concerning the handling of criminal cases of "debt-trap loans", in accordance with the Criminal Law, the Criminal Procedure Law, relevant judicial interpretations, and the provisions of normative documents such as the "Guiding Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Criminal Cases Involving Mafia-like Gangs and Criminal Syndicates" jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice:

I. Accurately Grasp the Distinction Between "Debt-Trap Loans" and Private Lending

1. "Debt-trap loans" is a general designation for related illegal and criminal activities in which, with the purpose of illegal possession, the perpetrator, under the guise of private lending, induces or forces the victim to sign a "loan" agreement or disguised "loan", "mortgage", or "guarantee" agreement, and creates false creditor-debtor relationships by means such as artificially inflating the loan amount, maliciously creating a default, arbitrarily determining a default, destroying or concealing evidence of repayment, and then illegally takes possession of the victim's property through litigation, arbitration, notarization, or the use of violence, threats, or other means.

2. There is an essential difference between "debt-trap loans" and civil lending relationships formed between equal subjects based on the principle of autonomy of will. The lender in private lending intends to recover the principal and obtain interest upon maturity in accordance with the content agreed upon in the agreement, and does not have the purpose of illegally possessing the property of others. Furthermore, the lender will not, during the process of signing or performing the loan agreement, engage in acts such as artificially inflating the loan amount, creating false evidence of payment, maliciously creating a default, arbitrarily determining a default, or destroying or concealing evidence of repayment.

In judicial practice, attention should be paid to distinguishing cases arising from illegal debt collection from cases of "debt-trap loans". If a criminal suspect or defendant does not have the purpose of illegal possession and does not use "traps" to form a false creditor-debtor relationship with the borrower, the case should not be regarded as a "debt-trap loan". If the act of forcibly demanding repayment through the use of violence, threats, or other means constitutes a crime, a conviction and punishment should be imposed based on the specific facts of the case.

3. In practice, the common criminal methods and steps of "debt-trap loans" include, but are not limited to, the following circumstances:

(1) Creating the illusion of private lending. Criminal suspects or defendants often advertise themselves in the name of "small loan companies", "investment companies", "consulting companies", "guarantee companies", or "online lending platforms", attracting victims to borrow money by using low interest rates, no collateral, no guarantee, or quick loan disbursement as bait. Subsequently, under false pretexts such as "security deposits" or "industry rules", they induce the victim, based on a mistaken understanding, to sign a "loan" agreement or related agreement with an artificially inflated amount. Some criminal suspects or defendants may also force the victim to sign a "loan" agreement or related agreement with an artificially inflated amount on grounds such as the victim's previous default on a loan.

(2) Creating false facts of payment such as fund transfer records. The criminal suspect or defendant transfers funds into the victim's account according to the artificially inflated amount in the "loan" agreement, creating bank transfer records showing that the entire loan has been delivered to the victim. Subsequently, they use various means to recover all or part of the funds, meaning the victim has not actually obtained or fully obtained the funds shown in the "loan" agreement or bank records.

(3) Intentionally creating a default or arbitrarily determining a default. Criminal suspects or defendants often intentionally cause the victim to default by setting default traps or creating obstacles to repayment, or by arbitrarily determining a default, thereby forcibly demanding that the victim repay a false debt.

(4) Maliciously stacking up the loan amount. When the victim is unable to repay, some criminal suspects or defendants may arrange for their own company or designated affiliated companies or persons to repay the "loan" on behalf of the victim, and then sign a new "loan" agreement or related agreement with a larger artificially inflated amount with the victim. Through this method of "transferring the note to settle the account" or "borrowing to repay a loan", the "debt" is continuously stacked up.

(5) Collecting the "debt" through both soft and hard tactics. When the victim fails to repay the artificially inflated "loan", the criminal suspect or defendant resorts to litigation, arbitration, notarization, or uses violence, threats, or other means to demand the "debt" from the victim or specific related persons of the victim.

II. Severely Punish "Debt-Trap Loan" Crimes in Accordance with the Law

4. In the process of committing a "debt-trap loan", if no obvious violent or threatening means are used, and the conduct is characterized overall as obtaining the victim's property by fraud through fabricating facts or concealing the truth with the purpose of illegal possession, the crime shall generally be convicted and punished as the crime of fraud. If multiple means are used concurrently during the commission of a "debt-trap loan", constituting multiple crimes such as fraud, extortion, illegal detention, false litigation, picking quarrels and provoking trouble, forced transaction, robbery, or kidnapping, the specific facts of the case shall be the basis for determining whether to impose concurrent punishment for multiple crimes or choose the heavier punishment in accordance with the Criminal Law and relevant judicial interpretations.

5. When multiple persons jointly commit a "debt-trap loan" crime, a criminal suspect or defendant who plays a principal role in the committed crime shall be deemed a principal offender and shall bear criminal responsibility for all crimes in which he participates or which he organizes or directs. A person who plays a secondary or auxiliary role shall be deemed an accessory.

A person who knows that another person is committing a "debt-trap loan" crime and is involved in any of the following circumstances shall be dealt with as an accomplice to the relevant crime, unless otherwise provided by the Criminal Law or judicial interpretations:

(1) Organizing the sending of "loan" information or advertisements, attracting or introducing victims to "borrow";
(2) Providing funds, premises, bank cards, accounts, means of transportation, or other assistance;
(3) Selling, providing, or assisting in obtaining citizens' personal information;
(4) Assisting in creating false payment records or other false facts of payment;
(5) Assisting in handling notarization;
(6) Assisting in filing lawsuits or arbitrations based on false facts;
(7) Assisting in cashing out, withdrawing cash, or handling the transfer of movable or immovable property, thereby transferring the criminal proceeds and the income derived therefrom;
(8) Other circumstances that meet the provisions on joint crimes.

The "knowledge that another person is committing a 'debt-trap loan' crime" in the above provisions shall be determined by comprehensively analyzing subjective and objective factors, including the perpetrator's cognitive ability, past experience, number of acts and methods, relationship with co-defendants or victims, profits obtained, whether he has been punished for "debt-trap loan" in the past, and whether he intentionally evades investigation.

6. When determining the amount of a "debt-trap loan" crime, it should be distinguished from private lending and evaluated negatively as a whole. The "artificially inflated debt" and the property illegally possessed by the criminal suspect or defendant under the names of "interest", "security deposit", "agency fee", "service fee", or "liquidated damages" shall all be included in the criminal amount.

The principal amount actually paid by the criminal suspect or defendant to the victim shall not be included in the criminal amount.

If a "debt-trap loan" has already been initiated but is not completed due to reasons beyond the perpetrator's control, a criminal attempt may be determined based on the amount of property already attempted to be illegally occupied, in accordance with the Criminal Law and judicial interpretations concerning the relevant charges. If there are both completed and attempted crimes, and the completed part and the attempted part correspond to different statutory sentencing ranges, it shall first be decided whether to impose a mitigated punishment for the attempted part, determine the statutory sentencing range for the attempted part, then compare it with the statutory sentencing range for the completed part, choose the heavier statutory sentencing range, and impose a heavier punishment as appropriate. If both are within the same sentencing range, a heavier punishment shall be imposed as appropriate based on the completed crime.

7. All property obtained as illegal gains by criminal suspects or defendants through "debt-trap loans" shall be recovered or ordered to be returned; the lawful property of victims shall be returned promptly. If there is evidence that the principal amount paid by the criminal suspect or defendant to the victim was for the purpose of committing a "debt-trap loan", any surplus after compensating the victim's losses shall be confiscated in accordance with the law.

If the criminal suspect or defendant has used the illegal gains to satisfy debts, transfer them, or create other encumbrances, recovery shall be made in accordance with the law under any of the following circumstances:

(1) A third party knowingly accepted the property as illegal gains;
(2) A third party obtained the illegal gains for free or at a price clearly lower than the market price;
(3) A third party obtained the illegal gains through the satisfaction of illegal debts or through illegal or criminal activities;
(4) Other circumstances under which recovery shall be made in accordance with the law.

8. If a "debt-trap loan" is targeted at elderly persons, minors, enrolled students, or persons who have lost the ability to work, or if the commission of a "debt-trap loan" causes the victim or a specific related person to commit suicide, die, become mentally disturbed, or commit criminal acts to repay the "debt", a heavier punishment shall be imposed as appropriate, unless otherwise provided by the Criminal Law or judicial interpretations.

While adhering to the principle of severe punishment in accordance with the law, a lighter punishment may be imposed in accordance with the law on a defendant who admits guilt and accepts punishment, actively returns stolen goods, genuinely repents, or has other statutory or discretionary mitigating circumstances.

9. For criminals involved in "debt-trap loans", the application of property-based penalties shall be strengthened in accordance with the specific crime committed. If the conditions under Article 37-1 of the Criminal Law are met, they may be prohibited from engaging in relevant occupations in accordance with the law.

10. A relatively fixed criminal organization formed by three or more persons for the purpose of committing "debt-trap loans" shall be identified as a criminal group. The ringleader shall be punished for all crimes committed by the group.

If the standards for identification as a mafia-like criminal syndicate or a criminal group of an evil force are met, the case shall be investigated, prosecuted, and tried as an organization of a mafia-like nature, an evil force, or a criminal group of an evil force.

III. Determine the Jurisdiction over Criminal Cases of "Debt-Trap Loans" in Accordance with the Law

11. Criminal cases of "debt-trap loans" shall generally be investigated by the public security organ at the place of the crime. If it is more appropriate for the public security organ at the place of residence of the criminal suspect to initiate the investigation, that public security organ may do so. The place of the crime includes the place where the criminal act occurred and the place where the criminal result occurred.

"The place where the criminal act occurred" includes the place where the company established for committing the "debt-trap loan" is located, the place where the "loan" agreement or related agreement was signed, the place where the illegal debt collection act was carried out, the place where the court, arbitration commission, or notary institution that accepted the litigation, arbitration, or notarization for committing the "debt-trap loan" is located, as well as the preparatory place, starting place, passing place, and ending place of the "debt-trap loan" act.

"The place where the criminal result occurred" includes the place where the illegal gains were paid, actually obtained, concealed, transferred, used, or sold.

In addition to the place of the crime and the place of residence of the criminal suspect, any public security organ in another place that receives a citizen's delivery, report, accusation, or tip-off, or receives a criminal suspect who surrenders himself, in connection with a "debt-trap loan" criminal case, shall immediately accept the case. After examination, if it finds that a crime exists, it shall transfer the case to the public security organ with jurisdiction for handling.

Criminal cases of "debt-trap loans" committed by mafia-like criminal syndicates or criminal groups of an evil force shall be investigated by the public security organ handling the case of the organization of a mafia-like nature, the evil force, or the criminal group of an evil force.

12. Under any of the following circumstances, the relevant public security organ may conduct a consolidated investigation within its scope of duties:

(1) A single person commits multiple crimes;
(2) It is a joint crime;
(3) A criminal suspect in a joint crime also commits other crimes;
(4) The crimes committed by multiple criminal suspects are directly related, and consolidated handling is conducive to ascertaining the facts of the case.

13. These Opinions shall take effect from April 9, 2019.
